info.name: Docusign Admin API
info.description:
# Docusign Admin API

The Docusign Admin API lets you manage organization-wide settings programmatically: users and memberships, accounts, identity providers, reserved domains, account/user imports and exports, account cloning and creation, data deletion, and Connect webhooks. This collection groups every endpoint into folders by domain and ships with ready-to-use OAuth flows so you can authenticate once and start calling APIs.

## What you can do here

- Manage users across one or many accounts (`eSignUserManagement`, `MultiProductUserManagement`, `Users`).
- Bulk import and export users and account settings (`UserImport`, `SingleAccountUserImport`, `UserExport`, `AccountSettingsImport`, `AccountSettingsExport`).
- Configure organization identity (`IdentityProviders`, `ReservedDomains`, `Organization`).
- Create and clone Docusign accounts (`AccountCreation`, `AccountCloning`).
- Subscribe to events with Docusign Connect (`Connect`).
- Permanently delete user data for compliance (`DataDeletion`).

## Authentication — pick one OAuth flow

The Admin API requires an OAuth 2.0 bearer token issued by Docusign's Account Server. Open the **🔐 Quick Auth Setup → Then Run APIs** folder and run one of these subflows once. Each flow stores an `access_token` variable that every other request uses automatically.

| Flow | Use when | Folder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JWT / Service Integration | Server-to-server, no user UI. Requires an RSA private key. | `01 - JWT / Service Integration` |
| Authorization Code Grant (Confidential Client) | Web app with a backend that can hold a client secret. | `02 - Authorization Code Grant (Confidential Client)` |
| Authorization Code Grant with PKCE | Public/native/SPA clients without a client secret. | `03 - Authorization Code Grant with PKCE (Public Client)` |

All flows must include the `signature` scope; admin endpoints additionally need scopes such as `organization_read`, `user_read`, `user_write`, `account_read`, `domain_read`, etc. Use the smallest scope set that satisfies your use case.

## Environments and variables

This collection is driven by environment variables. Pick or create an environment that defines:

| Variable | Purpose | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | Base URL for the Admin API. | `https://api.docusign.net/management` (prod) or `https://api-d.docusign.net/management` (demo) |
| `authServer` | Docusign Account Server. | `account.docusign.com` (prod) or `account-d.docusign.com` (demo) |
| `organizationId` | UUID of the target organization. | `0b3f5f3a-1c2e-4a4d-9b21-1d6d9f7e7a11` |
| `accountId` | Account UUID for account-scoped calls. | `c2d3e4f5-6789-4abc-90de-1234567890ab` |
| `userId` | User UUID for user-scoped calls. | `9c8b7a6d-5e4f-4321-a0b1-c2d3e4f56789` |
| `integrationKey` | Docusign Integration Key (client_id). | `e5b7…` |
| `redirectUri` | Redirect URI registered on your integration (Auth Code flows). | `https://oauth.pstmn.io/v1/callback` |
| `privateKey` | RSA private key for JWT flow. | (PEM contents) |
| `access_token` | Populated automatically after a successful OAuth run. | — |

The workspace already includes a **Docusign Admin API Environment**. Select it before running anything.

## First successful call (5 steps)

1. Select the **Docusign Admin API Environment** in the environment dropdown.
2. Set `integrationKey`, `organizationId`, and the auth-flow-specific values (`privateKey` for JWT, or `redirectUri` + client secret for Auth Code).
3. Open the auth subflow you chose under **🔐 Quick Auth Setup → Then Run APIs** and run the requests in order. The final request stores `access_token` in the environment.
4. Open **IdentityProviders → List identity providers for an organization** and send it. A `200 OK` with an `identity_providers` array confirms everything is wired up correctly.
5. From there, browse the folders by domain and start calling endpoints.

## Conventions used in this collection

- URLs use `{{baseUrl}}` and the relevant ID variables (`organizationId`, `accountId`, `userId`, `membershipId`, `importId`, etc.).
- Every request expects `Accept: application/json`.
- The collection's auth helper attaches `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}` to every call automatically; you do not need to set it per-request.
- Saved examples on each documented request show both a success response and a typical error so you know what to expect.

## Common errors at a glance

| Status | Meaning | Typical cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or expired token. | Re-run the OAuth subflow. |
| `403 Forbidden` | Token lacks required scope, or user is not an admin. | Re-issue the token with the correct scope and role. |
| `404 Not Found` | ID variable (org/account/user) does not exist or is not visible to the caller. | Verify the ID matches an entity the user can access. |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit hit. | Back off and retry; consider batching. |

## Reference

- Docusign Admin API guide: https://developers.docusign.com/docs/admin-api/
- OAuth flows: https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/

01 - JWT / Service Integration
01-1 - Construct Consent URL (JWT)

const integrationKey = u.getVar(pm, 'integrationKey', undefined, { required: true, aliases: ['IKey'] });

request.description:
## **Grant Consent for JWT (Impersonation)**

1. Execute this helper request.
    
2. Open the returned authorizeUrl in a browser.
    
3. Sign in and grant consent (must include `impersonation`).
    
4. After consent is granted, you can close the browser.
    
5. Run **01-2 - JWT Token (exchange)**.

item.name: 01-2 - JWT Token (exchange)

exec: // Require the caller to provide a ready-made JWT assertion
const custom = utils.getVar(pm, 'jwt_assertion', undefined, { required: true });
// Mint a new JWT assertion from key material
const integrationKey   = utils.getVar(pm, 'integrationKey',   undefined, { required: true, aliases: ['IKey'] });
const userId     = utils.getVar(pm, 'userId',     undefined, { required: true });
const authServer = utils.getVar(pm, 'authServer', undefined, { required: true });
const pem        = utils.getVar(pm, 'privateKey', undefined, { required: true });
const jwt = utils.mintJwt({ integrationKey, userId, authServer, privateKeyPem: pem, scope, expSeconds: 3600 });

request.description:
Exchanges the signed JWT (``{{​jwt_assertion}}``) for an access token.

**Two ways to supply the JWT assertion**
1) **Auto-mint (default):** Set ``{{​integrationKey}}`` (or ``{{​IKey}}``), ``{{​userId}}``, ``{{​authServer}}``, and ``{{​privateKey}}``. The script mints a JWT and sets ``{{​jwt_assertion}}`` for you.
2) **Custom assertion:** Set ``{{​USE_CUSTOM_ASSERTION}}`` to `true` **and** provide ``{{​jwt_assertion}}`` yourself (PEM not needed).

**Output:** ``{{​access_token}}``. (JWT does **not** return a refresh token.)

item.description:
This request demonstrates authentication using JSON Web Tokens (JWT) Grant for accessing APIs without user interaction. 1. Before making the first call, an administrator or the target user must grant consent to your **Integration Key** (Client ID) to allow specific scopes.To see the full list of all supported scopes, see [Authentication scopes](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/reference/scopes/). 2. Your server constructs and digitally signs a **JWT** using your **private key** and the user's ID. 3. The signed JWT is exchanged with the authorization server for a short-lived access token. This access token is then used in subsequent API calls. This workflow is ideal for background processes, scheduled tasks, and integrations that require impersonating a user without constant user interaction. **Variables** For context around what JWT Grant authentication is, when you should use it, and its advantages and disadvantages, see [JSON Web Token (JWT) Grant](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/jwt/). | Variable | Required | Notes | Default | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `{{​integrationKey}}` | ✅ | An integration key identifies your integration and links to its configuration values. [Create an integration key](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#how-to-get-an-integration-key).
Falls back to `{{​IKey}}`. | — | | `{{​userId}}` | ✅ | Find your [User ID](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#user-id) in the Apps and Keys page. | — | | `{{​privateKey}}` | ✅ | The **PEM formatted Private Key** used for RS256 signing the JWT. | — | | `{{​authServer}}` | ✅ | Authentication base URL (use [https://account.docusign.com](https://account.docusign.com) for Production). | `https://account-d.docusign.com` | | `{{​scope}}` | Optional | Permissions requested (e.g., signature, impersonation for JWT).To see the full list of all supported scopes, see [Authentication scopes](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/reference/scopes/). | `organization_read organization_write group_read user_read user_write account_read domain_read` | | `{{​USE_CUSTOM_ASSERTION}}` | Optional | `true` to use your own `{{​jwt_assertion}}` | `false` |

02-1 - Construct Authorization URL

exec: const authServer = u.getVar(pm, 'authServer', undefined, { required: true });
const integrationKey   = u.getVar(pm, 'integrationKey',   undefined, { required: true, aliases: ['IKey'] });

request.description:
## **Get the Authorization Code**

1. Execute the GET request of 02-1 - Construct Authorization URL.
    
2. Open the returned authorizeUrl and open in a browser tab.
    
3. Sign in, allow access and grant consent.
    
4. The browser will redirect to your redirectUri.
    
5. Copy the code value from the resulting URL query string.
    
6. Paste the copied code into a new or existing Environment or Collection Variable named ``{{​authCodeNoPkce}}``.

item.name: 02-2 - Exchange Authorization Code for Tokens

exec: // Accept either variables OR literal body params for these inputs:
// Resolve IKey/ISec fallback for {{integrationKey}}/{{clientSecret}} body templates
var _ik = utils.getVar(pm, 'integrationKey', null, { aliases: ['IKey'] }); if (_ik) pm.variables.set('integrationKey', _ik);
var _cs = utils.getVar(pm, 'clientSecret', null, { aliases: ['ISec'] }); if (_cs) pm.variables.set('clientSecret', _cs);

request.description:
## **Exchanging Code for Tokens**

This request exchanges the temporary Authorization Code for usable access and refresh tokens.

1. Verify that your environment or collection variables for ``{{​integrationKey}}`` (or ``{{​IKey}}``), ``{{​clientSecret}}`` (or ``{{​ISec}}``), and ``{{​authCodeNoPkce}}`` are all populated with the correct values.
    
2. Execute this request.
    
3. Check the response body: The response will contain the `access_token` and `refresh_token`.
    
4. The Pre-request or test script automatically extracts the access_token and refresh_token and saves them as environment variables. This lets you use the Bearer Token authentication instead of manual UI logins for later API calls.

item.description:
This folder implements the **Authorization Code Grant** flow. This process requires the user to be present initially to grant authorization through a browser-based login and consent screen.

Upon successful consent, the system receives an authorization code which is exchanged for both a short-lived access token and a long-lived refresh token.

The key benefit of this approach is the ability to use the refresh token to continually request new access tokens in the background, thereby maintaining long-lived user sessions and enabling your server to execute automated tasks without repeated user interaction.

**Variables**

Authorization Code Grant is a type of OAuth 2.0 flow used to obtain an access token. [Confidential Authorization Code Grant](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/authcode/#confidential-authorization-code-grant), which should be used by apps that can secure a secret key.

| Variable | Required | Notes | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ``{{​integrationKey}}`` | ✅ | An integration key identifies your integration and links to its configuration values. [Create an integration key](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#how-to-get-an-integration-key). Falls back to ``{{​IKey}}``. |  |
| ``{{​clientSecret}}`` | ✅ | The secret key identifies your integration app through a unique key. [Create a Secret Key](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#secret-key). Falls back to ``{{​ISec}}``. |  |
| ``{{​​redirectUri}}`` | ✅ | The URI is registered on your Docusign Integration Key (API Key). You can choose your application’s redirect uri. |  |
| ``{{​authServer}}`` | ✅ | Authentication base URL (use [https://account.docusign.com](https://account.docusign.com) for Production). | `https://account-d.docusign.com` |
| ``{{​​scope}}`` | Optional | Permissions requested (e.g., signature, impersonation for JWT).To see the full list of all supported scopes, see [Authentication scopes](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/reference/scopes/). | ``organization_read organization_write group_read user_read user_write account_read domain_read`` |
| ``{{​authCodeNoPkce}}`` | ✅ (Only on exchange) | Paste the `?code` here (env or collection var) |  |

item.name: 03 - Authorization Code Grant with PKCE (Public Client)
03-1 - Construct Authorization URL with PKCE

exec: const authServer = u.getVar(pm, 'authServer', undefined, { required: true });
const redirect   = u.encVar(pm, 'redirectUri', undefined, { required: true });
// prefer explicit publicIntegrationKey; otherwise require integrationKey
const integrationKey = pubId ? pubId : u.getVar(pm, 'integrationKey', undefined, { required: true, aliases: ['IKey'] });

const prompt = 'Open the URL, sign in, grant consent, copy ?code= and paste it into an **environment or collection variable** named "authCodePkce". Then run 03-2 - Exchange Authorization Code for Tokens (PKCE).';

request.description:
This request generates the authorization URL required to start the OAuth 2.0 flow.

## Get the Authorization Code

1. Execute the GET request of _03-1 - Construct Authorization URL with PKCE_.
    
2. Open the returned _authorizeUrl_ and open in a browser tab.
    
3. Sign in, allow access and grant consent.
    
4. The browser will redirect to your redirectUri.
    
5. Copy the _code_ value from the resulting URL query string.
    

Paste the copied _code_ into a new or existing Environment or Collection Variable named ``{{​authCodePkce}}``.

item.name: 03-2 - Exchange Authorization Code for Tokens (PKCE)

exec: // Client ID can be body literal (client_id) OR a variable (publicIntegrationKey/integrationKey)
throw new Error('Missing client id. Set publicIntegrationKey/integrationKey/IKey or place a literal client_id in the body.');
if (!hasPublicVar) { var _ik = utils.getVar(pm, 'integrationKey', null, { aliases: ['IKey'] }); if (_ik) pm.variables.set('publicIntegrationKey', _ik); }

request.description:
## Exchanging Code for Tokens

This request exchanges the temporary Authorization Code using PKCE for usable access and refresh tokens.

1. Verify that your environment or collection variables for ``{{​integrationKey}}`` (or ``{{​IKey}}``), ``{{​origin}}``, ``{{​authCodeWithPkce}}``, and the automatically generated ``{{​code_verifier}}`` are all populated with the correct values.
    
2. Ensure ``{{​origin}}`` matches the Origin registered on your Docusign Apps and Keys page and CORS is activated with all the HTTP operations. For further information, refer [Set the CORS configuration of your app.](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#cors-configuration)
    
3. Execute this request.
    
4. Check the response body: The response will contain the _access_token_ and _refresh_token_.
    
5. The Pre-request or test script should automatically extract and set the ``{{​access_token}}`` and ``{{​refresh_token}}`` variables for use in subsequent API calls.

item.description:
This folder implements the **Public Authorization Code Grant (with PKCE)** flow, which is the required OAuth 2.0 standard for public applications like Single Page Applications (SPAs) and mobile apps.

This process requires the user to be present initially to grant authorization through a browser-based login and consent screen.

Upon successful consent, the system receives an authorization code which is exchanged for both a short-lived access token and a long-lived refresh token.

The key benefit of this approach is the ability to use the refresh token to continually request new access tokens in the background, thereby maintaining long-lived user sessions and enabling your server to execute automated tasks without repeated user interaction.

**Variables**

Public Authorization Code Grant (with PKCE) is a type of OAuth 2.0 flow used to obtain an access token. [Public Authorization Code Grant](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/authcode/#public-authorization-code-grant), which does not require that your app secure a secret key.

| Variable | Required | Notes | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ``{{​publicIntegrationKey}}`` | ✅ | An integration key identifies your integration and links to its configuration values. [Create an integration key](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#how-to-get-an-integration-key). If absent, it falls back to ``{{​integrationKey}}``. |  |
| ``{{​integrationKey}}`` | Fallback | An integration key identifies your integration and links to its configuration values. Falls back to ``{{​IKey}}``. [Create an integration key](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#how-to-get-an-integration-key). |  |
| ``{{​redirectUri}}`` | ✅ | The URI is registered on your Docusign Integration Key (API Key). You can choose your application’s redirect uri. |  |
| ``{{​authServer}}`` | ✅ | Authentication base URL (use [https://account.docusign.com](https://account.docusign.com) for Production). | `https://account-d.docusign.com` |
| ``{{​origin}}`` | ✅ (Only on exchange) | The Origin URL registered in your Docusign App CORS configuration. Must match an allowed origin in Apps and Keys. See [Set the CORS configuration of your app.](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#cors-configuration) |  |
| ``{{​scope}}`` | Optional | Permissions requested (e.g., signature, impersonation for JWT).To see the full list of all supported scopes, see [Authentication scopes](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/reference/scopes/). | ``organization_read organization_write group_read user_read user_write account_read domain_read`` |

item.name: 04 - Refresh Access Token

exec: // Resolve IKey/ISec fallback for body/auth templates
var _ik = utils.getVar(pm, 'integrationKey', null, { aliases: ['IKey'] }); if (_ik) pm.variables.set('integrationKey', _ik);
var _cs = utils.getVar(pm, 'clientSecret', null, { aliases: ['ISec'] }); if (_cs) pm.variables.set('clientSecret', _cs);

request.description:
This request uses the long-lived refresh token to obtain a new access token, ensuring continuous API access without user re-authentication.

1. Verify that the ``{{​refresh_token}}`` variable is populated from the previous "Exchange Code for Tokens" request.
    
2. Execute this request.
    
3. The response will contain a brand new _access_token_.
    
4. The test script should automatically extract and overwrite the old value of the ``{{​access_token}}`` variable with the new token.

item.name: 05 - User Info

exec: pm.test('✅ Parsed userinfo (optional vars stored if present)', () => pm.expect(true).to.equal(true));

request.description:
The **User Info** request serves as the validation step following any successful OAuth 2.0 flow. It confirms the access token's validity and retrieves the fundamental identity details of your Docusign account.

- **Identity Validation:** The primary response fields, such as `"sub"` (the user ID), `"name"`, and `"email"`, confirms **who** the application is acting on behalf of.
    
- **API Configuration:.** The default account contains the `account_id` (`1b63b53e-xxxx-4728-xxxx-e5aef8f305d1`) and the correct `base_uri`. Your application must extract these values to construct the correct endpoints for making calls like sending envelopes or managing templates.
    

This request validates the entire authentication process and supplies all the required user and account context to interact with the Docusign API.

item.description:
This folder contains a curated set of requests for rapid Docusign integration. By configuring authentication at the folder level, you can execute all contained requests without manual per request setup. Successful execution of the authentication flows within this folder will populate the **Environment and Collection variables** `{{​access_token}}` and `{{​refresh_token}}`. Once these values are saved to your active environment, they will be globally available for all requests in this folder. Every request in this folder is configured with auth type as **inherit auth from the parent**. To ensure seamless execution, the folder itself is set to the **Bearer Token** authorization type, using `{{​access_token}}` as the value. **Note**: When viewing the Folder's **Authorization** tab, ensure the **Token** field contains only the variable `{{​access_token}}`. Do not include the word "Bearer" in the text box, as Postman automatically generates the correct `Authorization: Bearer [token]` header. ## **Choose your Authentication Type** Docusign uses OAuth 2.0 to secure your API requests. Using OAuth, your app requests access and performs actions, such as requesting a signature, on behalf of one of your users. Docusign provides four scenarios for implementing OAuth: - [Authenticate with the JWT Grant](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/jwt-get-token/) - [Authenticate with the Confidential Authorization Code Grant](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/confidential-authcode-get-token/) - [Authenticate with Public Authorization Code Grant](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/public-authcode-get-token/) - [Authenticate with Implicit Code Grant](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/implicit/) | Flow | When to use | Human present? | Client secret? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **JWT (Service Integration)** | Server/daemon jobs acting on behalf of a user after one-time consent has been granted. | No (after consent) | No (requires privateKey) | | **Confidential Authorization Code Grant** | Server-side applications that can securely store a secret. Supports refresh_token. | Yes (initial sign-in) | Yes | | **Public Authorization Code Grant (PKCE)** | SPA, Mobile, or Desktop apps that cannot securely store a secret. | Yes (initial sign-in) | No (uses PKCE flow) | ## Prerequisites Before obtaining the access token, ensure the following environment or collection variables are configured in Postman. | Variable | Example Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `{{​authServer}}` | Demo: [https://account-d.docusign.com](https://account-d.docusign.com)
Production: [https://account.docusign.com](https://account.docusign.com) | Authentication base URL. | | `{{​redirectUri}}` | [http://localhost:8080/](http://localhost:8080/) | A redirect URI (callback URI) where Docusign sends users after authentication. | | `{{​origin}}` | [https://localhost:3000](https://localhost:3000) | Origin URL for PKCE CORS requests. Must match an allowed origin in your Docusign [CORS configuration](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#cors-configuration). | | `{{​scope}}` | signature extended | Permissions requested (e.g., signature, impersonation for JWT). See: [https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/reference/scopes/](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/auth/reference/scopes/) | | `{{​integrationKey}}` | Example: f8db556a-xxxx-4f30-xxxx-648ea46axxxx | Integration key identifying your app (falls back to `{{​IKey}}`). Create one: [https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#how-to-get-an-integration-key](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#how-to-get-an-integration-key) | | `{{​clientSecret}}` | Example: f2db256a-xxxx-4f30-xxxx-64a2346axxxx | Secret key for confidential integrations (falls back to `{{​ISec}}`): [https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#secret-key](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#secret-key) | | `{{​publicIntegrationKey}}` | Example: f2db256a-xxxx-4f30-xxxx-64a2346axxxx | Public integration key used for PKCE flows. Falls back to `{{​integrationKey}}`/`{{​IKey}}`. | | `{{​userId}}` | Example: f2db256a-xxxx-4f30-xxxx-64a2346axxxx | User GUID. Find it here: [https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#user-id](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#user-id) | | `{{​privateKey}}` | \-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY----- ... -----END RSA PRIVATE KEY----- | RSA private key for JWT flow: [https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#rsa-key-pair](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#rsa-key-pair) | ## Steps to get token 1. JWT (Service Integration) 1. Open the **01 - JWT / Service Integration** folder. 2. Execute the GET request of **01-1 – Construct Consent URL**. 3. Open the returned **authorizeUrl** in a browser. 4. Sign in and grant consent (must include **impersonation**). 5. After consent is granted, you can close the browser. 6. Run **01-2 - JWT Token (exchange)** 2. Confidential Auth Code 1. Open the **02 – Authorization Code Grant (Confidential Client)** folder. 2. Execute the GET request of **02-1 – Construct Authorization URL**. 3. Open the returned **authorizeUrl** in a browser tab. 4. Sign in and grant consent. 5. Copy the **?code=** value from the URL and set it as `{{​authCodeNoPkce}}`. 6. Run **02-2 – Exchange Authorization Code for Tokens**. 3. Public Auth Code (PKCE) 1. Open the **03 – Authorization Code Grant with PKCE (Public Client)** folder**.** 2. Execute the GET request of **03-1 – Construct Authorization URL with PKCE**. 3. Open the returned **authorizeUrl** in a browser tab. 4. Sign in and grant consent. 5. Copy the **?code=** value from the URL and set it as `{{​authCodePkce}}`. 6. Ensure the Origin parameter added in Apps and Keys page is set in headers of **03-2 – Exchange Authorization Code for Tokens (PKCE)** and CORS is activated with all the HTTP operations. For further information, refer [Set the CORS configuration of your app.](https://developers.docusign.com/platform/configure-app/#cors-configuration) 7. Run **03-2 – Exchange Authorization Code for Tokens (PKCE)**. 4. Execute 05 – User Info to verify your user details and base URI. ## Notes - If the access token has expired, execute 04 – Refresh Access Token using the refresh token. Default expiration is 8 hours (`expires_in` is in seconds). - Moving to Production: Switch `{{​authServer}}` to [https://account.docusign.com](https://account.docusign.com) and re-consent. The base URI can be accessed by executing 05 – User Info.

exec: * utils: Shared helpers for the Auth folder (folder-level pre-request).
* These run before each request in this folder. Pass `pm` into helpers.
/** isString(v): true if v is a non-empty string */
const isString = v => typeof v === 'string' && v.trim() !== '';
/** isPlaceholder(v): true if value looks like a {{variable}} */
const isPlaceholder = v => isString(v) && v.startsWith('{{') && v.endsWith('}}');
/** asciiSafe(s): strip non-ASCII for header-safe echo endpoints */
return `Missing ${name}. Set it in your active Environment or in Collection variables.`;
* Resolve var from env → collection → globals, then try each alias.
function getVar(pm_, name, fallback, { required = false, aliases = [] } = {}){
if (required) { throw new Error(_missingMsg(aliases.length ? name + ' (or ' + aliases.join('/') + ')' : name)); }
/** encVar(pm, name, fallback, opt): getVar + encodeURIComponent (unless placeholder) */
const v = getVar(pm_, name, fallback, opt);

item.name: IdentityProviders
List identity providers for an organization

request.description:
# List identity providers for an organization

Returns the collection of identity providers (federated SSO connections such as SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect) configured for a Docusign organization. Use this to discover which IdPs exist before assigning them to a domain reservation, a user provisioning policy, or a federated authentication flow.

## Endpoint

`GET {{baseUrl}}/v2/organizations/{{organizationId}}/identity_providers`

## Authentication

This endpoint requires an OAuth 2.0 bearer token issued for the Docusign Admin API.

- Grant type: Authorization Code or JWT (see the collection-level auth configuration).
- Required scopes: at minimum `signature` and `organization_read`.
- The token must belong to a user with an Admin role in the target organization.

The collection passes the bearer token automatically when the auth helper variables (`authServer`, `integrationKey`, `clientSecret`, `redirectUri`, `scope`) are set.

## Required inputs

| Location | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Path | `organizationId` | UUID of the Docusign organization. Resolved from the `{{organizationId}}` environment variable. |
| Header | `Accept` | Must be `application/json`. |
| Header | `Authorization` | `Bearer <access_token>` — added automatically by the collection auth. |

No request body or query parameters are required.

## Successful response — `200 OK`

Returns an `identity_providers` array. Each entry describes a configured IdP:

- `id` — UUID of the identity provider.
- `name` — Human-readable label.
- `type` — `saml_2_0` or `open_id_connect`.
- `is_default` — Whether this IdP is the org-wide default.
- `auth_url` — The IdP authorization endpoint Docusign redirects users to.
- `created` / `modified` — ISO-8601 timestamps.

## Common errors

| Status | Meaning | Typical cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or expired bearer token. | Re-run the OAuth flow or refresh the token. |
| `403 Forbidden` | Token lacks `organization_read` scope or the user is not an Admin. | Re-issue the token with the correct scope and role. |
| `404 Not Found` | `organizationId` does not exist or is not visible to the caller. | Verify `{{organizationId}}` matches an org the authenticated user belongs to. |

## Try it

1. Set `baseUrl` (e.g. `https://api.docusign.net/management`) and `organizationId` in your active environment.
2. Ensure the collection-level OAuth is authorized.
3. Send the request — you should receive a `200 OK` with an `identity_providers` array.

item.name: Clone an existing Docusign account.

request.description:
Clones an existing Docusign account. Cloning an account copies the plan items and eSignature settings. Users, templates, and permission profiles are _not_ copied into the target account. The new account will linked to the same organization.

In the request body, specify the source account you are cloning by its ID. You can get the IDs for your organization's asset group accounts using the [getAssetGroupAccounts](/docs/admin-api/reference/accountprovisioning/accountcloning/getassetgroupaccounts/) endpoint. 

You also need to specify information about the new target account, including the name, location, and administrator. To set the location, provide either the `countryCode` or `region` properties. (If both are specified, the `region` value will be used.) When testing in the developer environment, the region will always be `NA`.

The request body looks like this:
```
{
    "sourceAccount": {
        "id": "624e3e00-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-43918c520dab"
    },
    "targetAccount": {
        "name": "My Cloned Account",
        "admin": {
            "firstName": "Francis",
            "lastName": "Beagle",
            "email": "francis@example.com"
        },
        "region": "NA"
    }
}
```

To call this endpoint:
* You must be an administrator for the specified organization. The administrator for the target account must also be an organization admin.
* The source account must be on the same plan as your contract.
* The source account must be an asset group account. An asset group is a set of modules, products, plans, and charges purchased for your organization. An asset group account is an account that has been linked to an asset group.
* Your organization must be set up for account cloning. For more information, email self-serve-provisioning-enablement@docusign.com.

[Required scopes](/docs/admin-api/admin101/auth/): `asset_group_account_clone_write`.

### Next steps
* See [how to use this endpoint to clone an account](/docs/admin-api/how-to/clone-account/).
